subject: Hosted vs incumbent: p95/p99 acceptance gates and streaming/concurrency next steps
body:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@aureliahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: latency targets post-demo

Thanks again for the demo this morning — useful discussion. A couple of quick follow-ups from our engineering team:

- We need clarity on how you measure end-to-end p95/p99 (client-side vs network vs server).
- Streaming behavior: for our voice->text->LLM pipeline we rely on partial outputs; can you guarantee p95 for first-byte streaming for short requests (<50 tokens)?
- Concurrency: current provider experiences spikes; our SLA requirement is p95 < 200ms and p99 < 600ms under steady 25 qps and 10% spikes to 60 qps for short windows (5-10 min).

I'll attach a traffic profile and a snapshot from our incumbent for reference. Let me know if you need anything else to scope a PoC.

—Tom
Director of Engineering, Aurelia Health

-----
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency targets post-demo

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachables. Recap and proposed next steps below so we have alignment before a short PoC: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Acceptance criteria requested: end-to-end p95 < 200ms, p99 < 600ms under your steady-state 25 qps and 10% spike profile.
- Streaming constraint: ensure first-byte (initial chunk) for short responses (<50 tokens) within p95 window.
- Measurement: you want the measurement to include network delta from our hosted API endpoint to your app edge (client -> Aurelia app -> Redwood hosted).

Clarifications from our side (questions)
- Can you confirm the geographic distribution of traffic (most sessions originate from US west coast)?
- What percent of requests are streaming versus full-response? (ballpark is fine).
- For spikes, are they single-shot bursts or many concurrent short-lived sessions?

Proposed next steps (outline)
1) Rapid 48-hour hosted PoC: Redwood runs your traffic profile against our hosted endpoints (we provide a sandbox API key and ephemeral metrics collection).
2) Measurement plan: Redwood will report client-visible p95/p99 using a lightweight agent script that you run from your edge to capture client-to-Redwood RTT and server-side logs for correlation.
3) Streaming test: we will run a focused streaming synthetic for short responses and measure first-byte latency percentiles.
4) Concurrency stress: included in PoC will be steady 25 qps and scheduled 10%/60 qps spike windows to match your profile.
5) Acceptance gating: if end-to-end p95 and p99 meet your targets in the 48-hour run and no functional regressions are detected, we proceed to a week-long canary with production tokens.

Deliverables from Redwood for PoC:
- Sandbox API key and endpoint
- PoC runbook and measurement script (single bash script + python collector)
- Raw percentile reports and a short slide summary (p95/p99, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization)

We can start as early as Monday if that works — tentative owners: me (PM), Karthik (latency/execution), Ben (commercial/contract).

If that alignment looks good, I'll send a short PoC statement of work and a drive folder with the measurement scripts.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

-----
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@aureliahealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency targets post-demo

Tom — quick tech clarifications so the PoC matches your production shape: 

1) Payloads: what is the average request size in tokens and the 95th percentile for token length? If voice pipeline, is there pre/post processing locally that adds latency?
2) TLS handshake: do you have persistent connections from your app to our endpoint or do you typically create short-lived connections per request? Persistent connections give better client-visible p95.
3) Retry policy: do you implement client-side retries on 5xx/timeouts? If so, supply the backoff window so we can emulate the same retry load.

From Redwood side: for streaming first-byte we will measure to the first chunk (typically within one network roundtrip + model compute for small tokens). For p99 we will surface both the client-observed percentile and our server-side histogram for debugging.

If you can share token distribution and connection patterns we will bake them into the PoC harness.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Performance | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@aureliahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency targets post-demo

Marissa / Karthik — thanks. Quick answers:
- Geography: ~78% US west, ~18% US central/east, ~4% APAC (very small).
- Streaming vs full: ~40% of requests are streaming (real-time), 60% are standard complete-response calls.
- Token sizes: median ~22 tokens, p95 ~85 tokens; voice preproc adds ~20ms on average.
- Connections: most of our services maintain persistent HTTP/2 connections but some mobile clients open short-lived connections.
- Retries: we have a simple retry for idempotent calls, exponential backoff starting at 50ms, max 3 attempts.

Attached: aurelia_traffic_profile_q4.csv and incumbent_p95p99_snapshot.pdf (incumbent numbers showing p95=230ms, p99=780ms under your runbook).

We can take the PoC next week — Monday or Tuesday preferred. Procurement will need a short PoC worksheet.

—Tom

Attachments: aurelia_traffic_profile_q4.csv (csv, 18KB); incumbent_p95p99_snapshot.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

-----
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@aureliahealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency targets post-demo — PoC kickoff and acceptance criteria

Tom — perfect, thanks for the data. Finalizing schedule and PoC SOW this morning. Quick summary of the acceptance gating we'll use for the 48-hour hosted run (so procurement has concrete wording):

PoC windows and measurement rules
- Run length: 48 hours continuous with the profile provided (steady 25 qps, scheduled spike windows to 60 qps per your CSV).
- Measurement points: client-observed p95 and p99 (we will give you the collector script to run on your edge) and Redwood server-side p95/p99 for correlation.
- Streaming first-byte gate: for requests <= 50 tokens, client-observed first-byte p95 must be < 200ms.
- Throughput gate: no sustained error rate > 0.5% and tail retries not exceeding 0.2% of requests.
- Resource telemetry: GPU utilization and queue lengths during spike windows; Redwood will provide these metrics in the raw report.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail)
- PASS if client-observed p95 <= 200ms AND p99 <= 600ms across the 48-hour run and error/ retry gates met.
- If PASS, proceed to 7-day canary with production keys and escalation playbook.
- If FAIL but within 10% of p95/p99 targets, agree to a follow-up engineering run (tuning: batching/quantization/kv-caching) and a second 24-hour test.

Next administrative items we will send today
- PoC SOW doc (one page) for Procurement to sign
- Sandbox API key and measurement script (Drive link)
- Calendar invite for kickoff + 30m pre-run tech check (we propose Tuesday 08:30 PT)

Ben — can you follow up with a clean PoC worksheet for Procurement (I copied procurement on the kickoff note)?

Tom — anything else you want explicitly in the SOW? If not, we’ll finalize and share the Drive link.

Thanks and talk soon,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
